Article.ArticleTitle: CORRELATION BETWEEN CEFEPIME UTILIZATION AND PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA RESISTANCE RATE TO BETA LACTAMS AND CARBAPENEMS IN PATIENTS WITH HEALTHCARE ASSOCIATED INFECTIONS.

Abstract.AbstractText: There is direct link between overutilization or abuse of antibiotics and P.aeruginosa resistance rate, but other factors could influence the resistance rate, too. The study aim was to observe changes of P.aeruginosa resistance rate in patients with hospital acquired infections (HAIs) after a period of cefepime unavailability in an intensive care unit (ICU).

The study was designed as retrospective observational analysis of trends in utilization of antibiotics and density of resistance to antibiotics. It covered only isolates P. aeruginosa causing HAIs and obtained from patients older than 18 years. Furthermore, the isolates taken less than 48h after admission to the ICU and duplicate isolates were excluded. Effects of cefepime withdrawal from prescribing during the two-years period on P.aeruginosa resistance density trends was also followed.

During the study period (2009-2016), a total of 318 non-duplicate isolates of P.aeruginosa causing HAIs in the ICU were collected. Dominant anatomical localization of these infections (nearly 95%) were lungs (pneumonia), surgical sites and urinary tract (69.18%, 18.24% and 6.92%, respectively). The isolates showed lower resistance density (per/1 000 PDs) in the last year (2016) compared to the first year of observation (2009) for all monitored antibiotics, with peak in 2011. Although decreasing trend of resistance density was recorded for all examined drugs, statistical significance was noted only for imipenem, meropenem and piperacillin/tazobactam (p<0.05) CONCLUSIONS: Temporary withdrawal of cefepime from utilization in a hospital results with significant decrease in density of P.aeruginosa isolates resistant to imipenem, meropenem, piperacillin/tazobactam, ceftazidime and cefepime.
